findings.cross_file_justification: cheval.py hard-aborts fallback traversal on ConfigError. The planner filters described in the review context do not remove agy from catalog fallback chains.
findings.description: The default-off gate introduces a hard configuration failure inside otherwise valid Google fallback chains. When an upstream HTTP hop fails and traversal reaches gemini-headless, the new ConfigError aborts the invocation instead of treating the disabled route as unavailable.
findings.failure_mode: Stock Google chains terminate with INVALID_CONFIG, masking the upstream failure. A custom chain with additional hops after gemini-headless never attempts those hops.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude non-opted-in agy hops during cheval chain construction, or explicitly handle AgyOptInRequiredError as a skipped hop while preserving the upstream failure when the chain is exhausted.

findings.cross_file_justification: The changed measured ceiling feeds the generated Bridgebuilder maxInput value of 916000, while Bridgebuilder admission estimates tokens using 0.25 tokens per character.
findings.description: The expanded Bridgebuilder budget mixes provider-measured tokens with character-based estimate units. The supplied calibration records approximately 1.8 times as many measured tokens for the probe filler, but the generated budget subtracts only 20000 from the measured ceiling without converting units.
findings.failure_mode: A large diff containing similarly tokenized content can pass admission at approximately 900000 estimated tokens while exceeding 1.6 million measured tokens. That exceeds the model's one-million-token context window, causing the review request to fail despite passing truncation.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert the measured ceiling into the estimator's units with a conservative margin, or use the model tokenizer for admission. Regenerate both source and distributed budgets and verify admission with content exhibiting the observed tokenizer ratio.

findings.cross_file_justification: The PR's own probe test documents that the filler is counted ~1.8x heavier by the Opus 4.7+ tokenizer than the chars/4.5 estimate; the generated Bridgebuilder budget (and dist/core/truncation.generated.js:31) lifts maxInput for claude-opus-5-5 from ~160K to 916000 in the same under-counting estimate units (0.25 tokens/char).
findings.description: The Bridgebuilder input budget is derived as catalog ceiling (936000, provider-measured tokens) minus 20000, but Bridgebuilder's maxInput is compared against a chars*0.25 estimate. The two units are not interchangeable: real diffs tokenize at roughly 3-3.5 chars/token, and the PR itself measured the probe filler at ~1.8x. A review admitted at ~900K estimated tokens can measure 1.1M-1.6M on the wire, above the 1M context window. The previous 160K budget had ~5x headroom to the window; the new budget sits at the window edge with zero margin for tokenizer skew.
findings.failure_mode: Any review whose estimated size lands between roughly 600K and 916K estimate-tokens passes Bridgebuilder truncation and cheval's (also estimate-based) ceiling check, then is rejected by the provider with 400 'prompt is too long'. The primary Opus 5.5 hop fails, the chain walks to claude-opus-5 whose 180K ceiling pre-empts it, and the review degrades or aborts exactly on the large diffs the budget exists to serve.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive maxInput from the measured ceiling divided by the observed tokenizer ratio (record['tokenizer_ratio'] from the probe, or a conservative 1.8), or keep the estimate-unit budget pinned to a value whose worst-case measured size stays under 1M (e.g. <=500000 estimate tokens). Add a test that maxInput * worst_case_ratio + default_max_tokens <= context_window.

findings.cross_file_justification: AgyOptInRequiredError subclasses ConfigError (INVALID_CONFIG, retryable=False). cheval's chain walk treats ConfigError as a hard abort, and the planner-side agy filters (_adv_agy_filter_chain, isAgyRouted, _tertiary_routes_to_agy) only gate explicitly planned hops, not catalog fallback_chain terminals.
findings.description: Every stock Google catalog chain terminates in gemini-headless, which is now the agy adapter with a default-off opt-in. On every existing deployment that has not added hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true, a chain walk that reaches that terminal after an upstream HTTP failure (rate limit, 5xx, ceiling) raises a non-retryable ConfigError from the fallback hop. The docstring claims planners read failure_class as 'not planned, never a failed voice', but nothing in the diff teaches the chain walk to skip a hop on failure_class == 'opt_in_required'; it only adds a new ConfigError subclass. This is a behavior change for hosts that have agy installed and previously completed via that terminal.
findings.failure_mode: An invoke whose primary and intermediate hops fail transiently exits INVALID_CONFIG with the agy opt-in message, masking the real upstream error. Operators see a config refusal for a model they never asked for, and retries/alerting keyed on the upstream failure class never fire.
findings.suggested_fix: In cheval's chain walk, treat a hop error carrying failure_class == 'opt_in_required' as 'hop not planned': skip it, keep the previous hop's error as the reported failure, and record the skip in MODELINV. Alternatively filter gemini-headless out of resolved fallback chains at plan time when agy_opt_in_enabled() is False, so the chain never reaches the refusal.

findings.cross_file_justification: resolve_effort returns a fourth source value 'extra' (CLI entries' legacy extra.effort), but the modelinv.py parameter comment (line 498), the cmd_invoke emit comment (line 2834) and the SDD D-2.3 wording all enumerate only caller | catalog | none. The trajectory payload schema (model-invoke-complete.payload.schema.json, in this PR) likely encodes that enum.
findings.description: Four values are produced where three are documented. If the payload schema restricts effort_source to an enum, every CLI-entry invoke that resolves via extra.effort emits a schema-invalid MODELINV record; if it does not, downstream consumers written to the documented tri-state silently mis-bucket 'extra'.
findings.failure_mode: Schema validation of model-invoke-complete fails (or telemetry consumers drop/misclassify) for headless hops whose effort came from extra.effort.
findings.suggested_fix: Either document and add 'extra' to the schema enum and all three comments, or collapse 'extra' into 'catalog' at the return site.

findings.description: Effort is resolved once against the primary (alias-followed) entry and placed on the single CompletionRequest shared by every hop. A catalog params.default_effort on the primary HTTP entry (e.g. xhigh on claude-opus-5-5) now flows unchanged to every fallback hop, including a claude-headless CLI hop where _effort_on_wire passes it straight through as --effort <level>. Before this change only an explicit --effort reached fallbacks. Conversely a fallback entry's own default_effort is never applied. effort_effective in MODELINV is recomputed from final_model_id but always with the primary's effort value.
findings.failure_mode: A fallback CLI hop receives an effort level chosen for a different model family; if the CLI rejects it (or the model does not support it) the hop fails instead of completing, and MODELINV records an effort_effective the answering hop never used when its own catalog default differed.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve effort per hop (call resolve_effort with the hop's entry inside the chain walk, preferring the explicit caller value), or at minimum only propagate a catalog-sourced effort to hops of the same provider family and record the per-hop source.

findings.cross_file_justification: The writer test pins that a claude-headless (Bedrock, global.anthropic.* model id) measurement is written into effective_input_ceiling of the anthropic:claude-opus-5-5 HTTP entry, and the floor test now asserts _lookup_max_input_tokens('anthropic', ...) returns that value for the direct-API route.
findings.description: A bound measured through a different transport and account (Claude Code CLI over Bedrock) is stamped on the direct HTTP entry as operator_set with method probed_headless. The direct API path's pre-emption at 180K protected accounts with per-minute input-token limits; a calibrated bound is by policy never lowered by observation, so the 936000 figure will persist for direct-API accounts whose real ITPM is far below it.
findings.failure_mode: Direct-API invocations up to ~936K tokens go on the wire and 429 against account ITPM limits (or 400 against the window after tokenizer skew) instead of being pre-empted locally; the chain walks and spend is incurred on the rejected attempt.
findings.suggested_fix: Record transport-specific ceilings (e.g. a claude-headless entry or a per-transport field) rather than overwriting the HTTP entry's effective_input_ceiling, or gate the HTTP route on account_limits.itpm when it is known and keep the 180K policy cap until an API-transport probe runs.

findings.description: The predicate deep-merges load_system_defaults(root) under the project config, so a headless.agy_opt_in: true in the framework-shipped System Zone defaults would opt every project in without any edit to .loa.config.yaml. The docstring says only ambient env is excluded, but the stated intent (operator's deliberate choice, argv exposure) argues for reading the project layer alone. The function also re-reads and re-parses both YAML files on every complete(), health_check() and validate_config() call.
findings.failure_mode: A future defaults update (or a tampered System Zone file) silently enables the argv-exposed agy route repo-wide; each agy dispatch also pays a full catalog parse.
findings.suggested_fix: Read only load_project_config(root) for this key (fail closed on exceptions as now) and memoize per project_root for the process lifetime.

findings.description: For measured entries the expectation becomes min(entry['effective_input_ceiling'], cw - dmt), so the equality assertion reduces to eic <= cw - dmt, which the following line already checks. The test no longer verifies anything about the measured value. Similarly test_write_operator_set_changes_only_the_entry_and_replaces_the_shortcut now skips permanently against the live catalog, so the only path exercising the real catalog layout is the SYNTH copy.
findings.failure_mode: A wrong or hand-edited effective_input_ceiling on a calibrated entry passes CI as long as it fits the window; the live-catalog writer path has no regression coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: For measured entries assert effective_input_ceiling == min(measured_input_tokens, cw - dmt) and probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling; replace the skip with a fixture that resets the live entry to its pre-probe shape before exercising the writer.

findings.description: The 'sets both' WARN fires whenever params.default_effort and extra.effort coexist, including HTTP entries where extra.effort is never consulted by any adapter (the docstring says so). It also fires when the caller passed an explicit --effort, where neither catalog value is used. The catalog check is strict (no normalization) while the extra path lower-cases and strips, so 'High' is rejected in params but accepted in extra.
findings.failure_mode: Spurious config-smell warnings on valid HTTP entries, and inconsistent acceptance of the same spelling across the two rungs.
findings.suggested_fix: Only warn when _is_cli_entry(entry) and no explicit effort was given; apply the same str().strip().lower() normalization to params.default_effort before validating.

findings.cross_file_justification: The test fixture deliberately deletes ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before every CLI-transport run, which is the only reason the recorded host_route/cli_model provenance is stable; the probe itself passes the inherited os.environ rather than the adapter's build_headless_subprocess_env().
findings.description: With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present in the operator's shell, the Claude Code CLI will authenticate with the key and route to the direct API, while the probe records host_route and cli_model as Bedrock/subscription from the wrapper env variables it inspects. The written reprobe_trigger and provenance line then describe a transport the measurement never used, and the spend lands on the API key rather than the subscription.
findings.failure_mode: Catalog provenance for an operator_set bound is wrong, and the budget guard underestimates real cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Spawn the CLI with build_headless_subprocess_env() (as the adapter does) plus the probe's own additions, and refuse or warn when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set while --transport claude-headless is selected.

findings.cross_file_justification: The schema description states measured_input_tokens is the value written to probed_ceiling; the clamp test pins probed_ceiling == 936000 while measured_input_tokens == 972887 for the same entry.
findings.description: The v3 schema's human-readable contract for measured_input_tokens contradicts the fr23b clamp the writer now applies. Tooling or operators following the schema text will expect probed_ceiling == measured_input_tokens and read the shipped catalog entry (and any future clamped write) as corrupt or hand-edited.
findings.failure_mode: Catalog consumers that validate the measured/probed relationship per the schema description reject or mis-handle clamped entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the schema description to 'the raw accepted size; probed_ceiling and effective_input_ceiling are min(this, context_window - default_max_tokens)', and add a schema-level or loader-level check for that relationship.
